title: Friday: salawat
hook: send many blessings on the Prophet ﷺ on Friday (Abu Dawud)
tomorrow: why would anyone skip lunch on an ordinary Thursday?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the hidden hour: not a code to crack, but a reason to keep asking. Today Friday gets a sound, and you can count it on your hand.

Behind a coffee counter there's a rhythm: the grinder, the tamp, the hiss of the milk. On a Friday, in some Muslim homes and shops, another rhythm runs underneath it, said softly: Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad. O God, send blessings on Muhammad. Then again. And it's counted, not on a screen, but on the fingers, the thumb stepping from joint to joint.
screen: `GRIND, TAMP, HISS.` → `A SOFT LINE UNDERNEATH.` → `COUNTED ON THE FINGERS.`

segments.voice: That's salawat, sending blessings on the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and Friday is its day. In a report in Sunan Abi Dawud, he calls Friday among the best of your days, and says: send many blessings on me on it, for your blessing is shown to me. The Qur'an sets the pattern first, in Pickthall's words: "Lo! Allah and His angels shower blessings on the Prophet. O ye who believe! Ask blessings on him and salute him with a worthy salutation." Notice the order. God and the angels already do it; people are invited into a sound that's already going. A report in Sahih Muslim adds a kind of arithmetic of mercy: whoever sends one blessing on him, God sends ten on that person. And the fingers? In another report in Abu Dawud, the Prophet tells a group of women to count their dhikr, their remembrance, on their fingertips, because the fingers will be asked, and made to speak. Here's the detail worth telling a friend tonight: in that picture, your hands are witnesses. Each joint you touch while saying the words becomes a small record of the day. None of it needs a mosque or a microphone; it can run quietly under the noise of a working day. Friday blessings, then, are a sound you make and a count you can feel.
screen: `AMONG THE BEST OF YOUR DAYS.` · `GOD AND THE ANGELS FIRST.` · `ONE BLESSING, TEN BACK.` · `FINGERS AS WITNESSES.` · then, large: `FRIDAY BLESSINGS.`

segments.voice: Rest one hand open on your knee. With your thumb, touch each joint of your fingers in turn, and with each touch say softly, Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad, or simply listen to the words if they aren't yours to say. Keep the count going as long as the sit runs, toward a hundred if the day allows.
screen: `ONE HAND OPEN.` · `THUMB TO EACH JOINT.` · `ONE LINE, EACH TOUCH.`

segments.voice: Friday's salawat: the words asking God to bless the Prophet, sent many times on Friday and counted, joint by joint, on the hand.
Your line, said softly: friday blessings join a sound God and the angels started first. Four days, four ways into Friday.

howItsDone: On Fridays, Muslims send salawat on the Prophet, saying a short formula such as Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad again and again, alone or in a group, counting on the fingers or on prayer beads.

fork.setup: your little cousin asks why grandma keeps moving her thumb across her fingers while she whispers. what's a true, simple answer?
